workItem.title: Characterize symbol and object statuses without coercion
workItem.body:
Add one characterization test for the existing summarize behavior. This verifies the accepted counter contract; preserve production behavior.

Acceptance:
- Append one test to src/summary.test.mjs, preserving all 31 existing tests byte-for-byte as a prefix and preserving src/summary.mjs exactly.
- Use a frozen inventory with exact primitive passed and failed statuses, a Symbol status, and a frozen object status whose string conversion throws. Expect literal counters total=4, passed=1, failed=1, unavailable=2 without coercing either unusual status.
- Verify the inventory and each status identity are preserved. Existing verification and the conventional branch guard must pass unchanged.
- During implementation, preserve product models, provider metadata, implementation policy and workflow configuration. Planning artifacts for this issue are allowed; the accepted product definition covers this behavior.

Verification phases: execute the declared candidate checks through the trusted host. Completion claims must cite their actual receipts. Validation of the eventual named published branch and forge CI are subsequent host gates; record those as pending before publication rather than claiming they already ran.

Operator acceptance exercises Lighthouse #541 with controlled default-branch advances around final-review dispatch. The isolated control grants no additional implementation, merge, CI retry or ProductShape apply. The initial seed stopped safely before publication when independent review found unsupported check claims; the operator is adding the missing required checks before a fresh execution.

Six independent host checks passed under published SDLC 0.21.11, the actual conventional published branch passes Lighthouse and its branch guard, and Consumer verification passed. The issue-specific OpenSpec plan preserves host metadata and makes no product-model or policy change. Approve this exact implementation for the normal integration route; final acceptance remains a separate automatic post-merge review.
